content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To size jeans, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Document final waist measurement (2 minutes)
Step 2. Note the rise height preference (3 minutes)
Step 3. Measure the front rise (1 minute)
Step 4. Lay jeans flat on a hard surface (30 seconds)
Step 5. Locate a flexible measuring tape (5 minutes)
Step 6. Smooth out wrinkles in the fabric (1 minute)
Step 7. Pull the waistband taut (45 seconds)
Step 8. Compare measurements to a size chart (10 minutes)
Step 9. Measure the inseam from crotch to hem (2 minutes)
Step 10. Record the hip width (1 minute)
Step 11. Unroll the pant legs completely (15 seconds)
Step 12. Button the fly or zip the zipper (20 seconds)
Step 13. Double check all recorded numbers (5 minutes)
Step 14. Identify the material composition (1 minute)
Step 15. Determine the desired leg opening width (2 minutes)
Step 16. Calculate the average of two waist readings (3 minutes)
Step 17. Measure the back rise (1 minute)
Step 18. Align the front and back waistbands (30 seconds)
Step 19. Check for fabric shrinkage allowance (15 minutes)
Step 20. Shake out the jeans to reset the seams (10 seconds)
Step 21. Write down the thigh circumference (1 minute)
Step 22. Measure the leg opening across the bottom (45 seconds)
Step 23. Measure the distance across the waistband (30 seconds)
Step 24. Measure the total length from waist to floor (2 minutes)
Step 25. Locate the crotch seam intersection (15 seconds)
Step 26. Finalize the size recommendation (5 minutes)
Step 27. Measure the width of the hips (1 minute)
Step 28. Measure the width of the thigh (45 seconds)
Step 29. Clear a large workspace on a table (2 minutes)
Step 30. Ensure the measuring tape is not twisted (10 seconds)
Step 31. Research brand-specific vanity sizing (20 minutes)
Step 32. Measure the knee width (1 minute)
Step 33. Read the care label for stretch content (2 minutes)
Step 34. Identify the style of the cut (1 minute)
Step 35. Account for the fabric's elastane percentage (4 minutes)
Step 36. Adjust for high-waisted vs low-waisted fit (3 minutes)
Step 37. Inspect the leg seams for straightness (1 minute)
Step 38. Note the flare or taper of the leg (1 minute)
Step 39. Measure the outseam length (2 minutes)
Step 40. Stretch the denim to check for elasticity (30 seconds)
